text:
maya: noticed customer reports of unexpected 429/503 spikes this morning even though meter-pipeline shows normal usage. looks like enforcement is firing faster than recorded usage. anyone else seeing disconnects?

devin: seeing same. enforcement logs show burst tokens consumed, but metering consumer lag is ~3m on kinesis. enforcement uses recent aggregated counts, pipeline is async -> potential race.

li: confirmed: metering-agg lag histogram + enforcer write path mismatch. query: `select sum(tokens) from metering_agg where window_start >= now()-5m and org='acme'` returns lower than enforcer reads from redis counter.

sasha: kinesis-consumer lag spikes correlated with a deploy at 03:10 UTC (consumer restart). consumer restarted but rebalanced slow -> backlog. backlog makes pipeline behind so reconciliation sees lower ingestion. enforcer reads fast store (redis/rolling-buckets) that includes bursts that metering job hasn't aggregated into long-term store yet.

ingest-bot: ALERT: metering-consumer group lag > 400k records for 15m (stream: usage-events).

gbarnes: root cause looks like: (1) transient consumer lag after deploy, (2) enforcer relies on fast rolling counters + enforcement window semantics, (3) reconciliation/backfill assumes eventual consistency and runs hourly -> too slow for bursty clients.

maya: agreed. short-term mitigation? we need to avoid billing/penalizing customers while pipeline catches up. options: relax enforcement grace window, bump per-key burst cap temporarily, or route heavy customers to dedicated capacity.

devin: propose immediate mitigation: set enforcer grace_tokens=5000 for org-tier=standard for next 30m and enable shadow-mode enforcement logging (no hard throttles) for a subset of traffic to measure divergence. I'll push a small flag.

li: +1 but we should also add a quick reconciliation job to replay aggregate counts into redis so enforcer sees consistent totals. can run as one-off while consumer catches up. I can script a replay using the s3 raw events.

sasha: we should also make the consumer liveness check stricter and avoid rolling restart in that path until we have graceful handoff. opened a small PR to add consumer draining + restart-backoff.

gbarnes: medium-term fixes we discussed before but let's write them down: 1) make enforcer read from a pre-aggregated fast-store with deterministic sequence ids (no dual-source read), 2) make metering pipeline produce a compact streaming aggregate (per-org, per-key, seq) that enforcer can tail with low-latency, 3) add a reconciliation worker that compares enforcer counters vs agg store and issues corrective credits/alerts.

maya: concrete action items:
- devin: enable temporary grace_tokens + shadow-mode flag (owner: devin)
- li: run one-off replay from raw events into redis counters (owner: li)
- sasha: patch consumer restart logic and rollout (owner: sasha)
- gbarnes: draft design doc for pre-aggregated tailable stream + reconcile worker (owner: gbarnes)

devin: will flip grace_tokens and enable shadow-mode in prod within 10m, will post rollback plan.

li: starting replay now: snippet I'm running:
```
python replay_rebuild.py --src s3://raw-metering/2027-06-01/ --dest redis://enforcer:6379/0 --org acme --window 5m
```

sasha: consumer PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/consumers/pull/857 - adds drain on SIGTERM + exponential backoff on rebalance. will stage to canary cluster first.

ingest-bot: NOTE: one-off replay job started by li (job-id: replay-20270601-17), estimating 8m runtime.

maya: good. also let's add a short-term dashboard tile in console showing enforcer counter vs metering-agg for top 50 orgs so SRE can spot divergence early. can we get a graph within today?

gbarnes: I can wire a grafana panel to query redis vs metering_agg. will add alert if delta > 10% for >2m.

devin: update: grace_tokens applied, shadow-mode on for 10% traffic, logging increased. rolling back if errors.

li: replay finished, pushed ~1.2M token events to redis, enforcer counters are now within expected bounds for acme. verifying customer reports cleared.

maya: awesome. leave this thread open until design doc + consumer patch merged. we'll follow-up with postmortem notes. :thumbsup:

gbarnes: creating design doc draft now - will link in #eng-platform when ready.

sasha: PR merged to canary, looks healthy. scheduling prod rollout in 30m with pause window.

ingest-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: consumer group lag dropped below 5k.

maya: thanks all — summary: transient consumer lag + dual-source reads caused enforcement vs metering divergence. short-term: grace tokens + replay + consumer restart fix. medium-term: single pre-agg tailable stream + reconciliation worker. owners assigned.
